paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: wisdom is better than strength. The Teacher saw a small city with few men, and a mighty king came against it. The city wasn't saved by muscle or weapons. A poor wise man saved it by his wisdom (Ecclesiastes 9:14-15). And then nobody remembered him, which tells you the world doesn't always hand out medals for the right things.

So how do you live that out? Slow down, baker, and get skilled instead of just working harder. The Teacher says, "If the axe is dull and the blade unsharpened, more strength must be exerted, but skill produces success" (Ecclesiastes 10:10). He says the calm words of the wise are heeded over the shouts of a ruler among fools (Ecclesiastes 9:17), and I say that as the LOUDEST stamper in the Dorinverse. Gracious words, steady hands and honest work beat noise every time. Tiny folly can spoil a lot too, like dead flies in the perfumer's oil (Ecclesiastes 10:1), so guard the little things.

Here's the part that matters most: wisdom doesn't always get a parade, and that's okay. Your good choices might go unnoticed, just like that poor man's. But the Teacher called that wisdom great (Ecclesiastes 9:13), and it still saved the city. So keep sharpening the axe, baker, keep your words gracious, and keep showing up at your post, whether anybody claps or not.
